1	# Feature Specification: Kanban Core — Board, Lane, Card, and Membership Management
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `002-kanban-core`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-06-01
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "The rest of the Kanban application beyond auth/onboarding (already specced as 001-auth-onboarding). Need to spec: board management, lane management, card management, board membership/invites, drag-and-drop reordering. The repo structure and constitution are already established."
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Admin Creates a Board and Adds Lanes (Priority: P1)
14	
15	The administrator — the first user in the system — creates a new board to organize work. They give the board a name and then add an initial set of ordered columns (lanes), such as "To Do," "In Progress," and "Done." Creating a board automatically makes the admin its owner. Until at least one board with lanes exists, there is nothing for members to collaborate on.
16	
17	**Why this priority**: A board with at least one lane is the prerequisite for every other feature in this spec. Nothing else works until a board exists.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Sign in as admin, create a board with a name, add three lanes to it in order, retrieve the board, and confirm all three lanes appear in the correct order with the correct names. Confirm the admin is listed as the board's owner.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** the admin is signed in, **When** they submit a valid board name, **Then** the system creates the board, assigns the admin as its owner, and returns a summary including the new board's identifier and name.
24	2. **Given** the admin has created a board, **When** they add a lane with a name to that board, **Then** the lane is appended at the end of the lane list with the next available position and the board's lane list reflects the addition immediately.
25	3. **Given** a board has three lanes named "To Do," "In Progress," and "Done," **When** a member retrieves the board, **Then** the lanes appear in the order they were created.
26	4. **Given** the admin is signed in, **When** they attempt to create a board with an empty name or a name exceeding 200 characters, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear validation message and no board is created.
27	5. **Given** a registered user who is not an admin, **When** they attempt to create a board, **Then** the request is refused with a permission-denied response.
28	6. **Given** the admin already has a board named "Sprint Board," **When** they attempt to create another board with the same name, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear message that a board with that name already exists.
29	
30	---
31	
32	### User Story 2 - Board Member Adds and Manages Cards (Priority: P1)
33	
34	A board member (owner or member role) adds work-item cards to lanes. Each card has at minimum a title; optionally a description and a due date. Members can edit an existing card's title, description, and due date. Members can also delete cards that are no longer needed. Viewers can see all cards but cannot create, edit, or delete them.
35	
36	**Why this priority**: Cards are the atomic unit of work in a Kanban board — the product delivers zero value without them.
37	
38	**Independent Test**: Sign in as a board member, add a card with a title and description to a lane, retrieve the lane's cards and confirm the card appears. Edit the card's title, confirm the change persists. Delete the card, confirm it no longer appears and the remaining cards' positions are gapless.
39	
40	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
41	
42	1. **Given** a board member is viewing a lane, **When** they submit a new card with a title, **Then** the card is added to the bottom of the lane's card list and the response includes the card's identifier and its assigned position.
43	2. **Given** a card exists in a lane, **When** a board member submits an update with a new title, description, and due date, **Then** all three values are persisted and subsequent retrieval reflects the updated values.
44	3. **Given** a card has a due date set, **When** a board member submits an update clearing the due date, **Then** the due date is removed and subsequent retrieval shows no due date on that card.
45	4. **Given** a card exists, **When** a board member deletes it, **Then** the card is removed from the lane and the remaining cards in that lane have their positions adjusted to remain gapless.
46	5. **Given** a board viewer (not owner or member), **When** they attempt to create, update, or delete a card, **Then** the request is refused with a permission-denied response.
47	6. **Given** a member submits a card with an empty title or a title exceeding 200 characters, **When** the system validates the request, **Then** it is rejected with a clear message and no card is created or modified.
48	
49	---
50	
51	### User Story 3 - Member Reorders Cards and Lanes via Drag-and-Drop (Priority: P1)
52	
53	A board member rearranges the board visually. They can drag a card to a new position within its current lane (changing its order among sibling cards), drag a card to a different lane (moving the work item to a new stage), and drag a lane to a new position (reordering the columns). Keyboard users can accomplish the same moves without a mouse. Changes are applied immediately in the UI and persisted so that anyone who loads the board next sees the updated order.
54	
55	**Why this priority**: Reordering is the primary daily interaction for Kanban users — it represents moving work through the workflow. A board where everything is stuck in a fixed order is not a kanban board.
56	
57	**Independent Test**: Load a board with two lanes and at least three cards in the first lane. Drag the bottom card to the top of the first lane; confirm the order changes immediately. Drag the first card from the first lane to the second lane; confirm it appears there. Drag the second lane to the first position; confirm the column order changes. Reload the board and confirm all reorderings persisted. Repeat all moves using keyboard controls only.
58	
59	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
60	
61	1. **Given** a lane has cards in positions 1, 2, 3, **When** a board member moves the card at position 3 to position 1, **Then** the moved card occupies position 1, the former positions 1 and 2 shift to 2 and 3 respectively, and the new order is persisted.
62	2. **Given** a card exists in Lane A at position 2 of 3, **When** a board member moves it to Lane B at position 1 of 2, **Then** the card is removed from Lane A (remaining cards' positions adjust), the card appears in Lane B at position 1 (existing Lane B cards shift down), and the change is persisted.
63	3. **Given** a board has three lanes, **When** a board member drags the third lane to the first position, **Then** the lane ordering updates so the moved lane is first, the other lanes shift right, and the order persists on reload.
64	4. **Given** a board member is using keyboard navigation, **When** they use the keyboard drag interface to move a card or lane, **Then** the same positional changes and persistence rules apply as for pointer-based drag.
65	5. **Given** a board viewer, **When** they attempt to drag any card or lane, **Then** the drag is not initiated and no reordering occurs.
66	6. **Given** two members submit moves for the same card simultaneously, **When** both requests reach the system, **Then** exactly one succeeds and the other receives a conflict response prompting a refresh; the final board state is consistent with exactly one winner.
67	
68	---
69	
70	### User Story 4 - Board Owner Invites and Manages Board Members (Priority: P2)
71	
72	A board owner (or system admin) invites a person to collaborate on a specific board by specifying the person's email address and the role they should have: Owner, Member, or Viewer. The system issues a single-use time-limited invitation link. When the invitee accepts, they become a registered user of the system (if they are not already one) and are immediately added to the board with the assigned role. The owner can also change a member's role or remove a member from the board after they have joined.
73	
74	**Why this priority**: Collaboration is the entire point of a Kanban board — a solo board is a to-do list. But the core board experience from US1–US3 can be demonstrated solo first, making this P2.
75	
76	**Independent Test**: Sign in as a board owner, issue a board invitation for a new email with the Member role. Accept the invitation with a matching Google account. Confirm the new user appears in the board's member list with the Member role and can add cards. Change their role to Viewer and confirm they can no longer add cards. Remove them from the board and confirm they no longer appear in the member list and receive a not-found response when accessing the board.
77	
78	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
79	
80	1. **Given** a board owner is signed in, **When** they invite `newperson@example.com` to a board with the Member role, **Then** the system records a pending board membership for that email and role and returns a redemption link the owner can share.

# Feature Specification: Kanban Core — Board, Lane, Card, and Membership Management

**Feature Branch**: `002-kanban-core`

**Created**: 2026-06-01

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "The rest of the Kanban application beyond auth/onboarding (already specced as 001-auth-onboarding). Need to spec: board management, lane management, card management, board membership/invites, drag-and-drop reordering. The repo structure and constitution are already established."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Admin Creates a Board and Adds Lanes (Priority: P1)

The administrator — the first user in the system — creates a new board to organize work. They give the board a name and then add an initial set of ordered columns (lanes), such as "To Do," "In Progress," and "Done." Creating a board automatically makes the admin its owner. Until at least one board with lanes exists, there is nothing for members to collaborate on.

**Why this priority**: A board with at least one lane is the prerequisite for every other feature in this spec. Nothing else works until a board exists.

**Independent Test**: Sign in as admin, create a board with a name, add three lanes to it in order, retrieve the board, and confirm all three lanes appear in the correct order with the correct names. Confirm the admin is listed as the board's owner.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the admin is signed in, **When** they submit a valid board name, **Then** the system creates the board, assigns the admin as its owner, and returns a summary including the new board's identifier and name.
2. **Given** the admin has created a board, **When** they add a lane with a name to that board, **Then** the lane is appended at the end of the lane list with the next available position and the board's lane list reflects the addition immediately.
3. **Given** a board has three lanes named "To Do," "In Progress," and "Done," **When** a member retrieves the board, **Then** the lanes appear in the order they were created.
4. **Given** the admin is signed in, **When** they attempt to create a board with an empty name or a name exceeding 200 characters, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear validation message and no board is created.
5. **Given** a registered user who is not an admin, **When** they attempt to create a board, **Then** the request is refused with a permission-denied response.
6. **Given** the admin already has a board named "Sprint Board," **When** they attempt to create another board with the same name, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear message that a board with that name already exists.

---

### User Story 2 - Board Member Adds and Manages Cards (Priority: P1)

A board member (owner or member role) adds work-item cards to lanes. Each card has at minimum a title; optionally a description and a due date. Members can edit an existing card's title, description, and due date. Members can also delete cards that are no longer needed. Viewers can see all cards but cannot create, edit, or delete them.

**Why this priority**: Cards are the atomic unit of work in a Kanban board — the product delivers zero value without them.

**Independent Test**: Sign in as a board member, add a card with a title and description to a lane, retrieve the lane's cards and confirm the card appears. Edit the card's title, confirm the change persists. Delete the card, confirm it no longer appears and the remaining cards' positions are gapless.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a board member is viewing a lane, **When** they submit a new card with a title, **Then** the card is added to the bottom of the lane's card list and the response includes the card's identifier and its assigned position.
2. **Given** a card exists in a lane, **When** a board member submits an update with a new title, description, and due date, **Then** all three values are persisted and subsequent retrieval reflects the updated values.
3. **Given** a card has a due date set, **When** a board member submits an update clearing the due date, **Then** the due date is removed and subsequent retrieval shows no due date on that card.
4. **Given** a card exists, **When** a board member deletes it, **Then** the card is removed from the lane and the remaining cards in that lane have their positions adjusted to remain gapless.
5. **Given** a board viewer (not owner or member), **When** they attempt to create, update, or delete a card, **Then** the request is refused with a permission-denied response.
6. **Given** a member submits a card with an empty title or a title exceeding 200 characters, **When** the system validates the request, **Then** it is rejected with a clear message and no card is created or modified.

---

### User Story 3 - Member Reorders Cards and Lanes via Drag-and-Drop (Priority: P1)

A board member rearranges the board visually. They can drag a card to a new position within its current lane (changing its order among sibling cards), drag a card to a different lane (moving the work item to a new stage), and drag a lane to a new position (reordering the columns). Keyboard users can accomplish the same moves without a mouse. Changes are applied immediately in the UI and persisted so that anyone who loads the board next sees the updated order.

**Why this priority**: Reordering is the primary daily interaction for Kanban users — it represents moving work through the workflow. A board where everything is stuck in a fixed order is not a kanban board.

**Independent Test**: Load a board with two lanes and at least three cards in the first lane. Drag the bottom card to the top of the first lane; confirm the order changes immediately. Drag the first card from the first lane to the second lane; confirm it appears there. Drag the second lane to the first position; confirm the column order changes. Reload the board and confirm all reorderings persisted. Repeat all moves using keyboard controls only.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a lane has cards in positions 1, 2, 3, **When** a board member moves the card at position 3 to position 1, **Then** the moved card occupies position 1, the former positions 1 and 2 shift to 2 and 3 respectively, and the new order is persisted.
2. **Given** a card exists in Lane A at position 2 of 3, **When** a board member moves it to Lane B at position 1 of 2, **Then** the card is removed from Lane A (remaining cards' positions adjust), the card appears in Lane B at position 1 (existing Lane B cards shift down), and the change is persisted.
3. **Given** a board has three lanes, **When** a board member drags the third lane to the first position, **Then** the lane ordering updates so the moved lane is first, the other lanes shift right, and the order persists on reload.
4. **Given** a board member is using keyboard navigation, **When** they use the keyboard drag interface to move a card or lane, **Then** the same positional changes and persistence rules apply as for pointer-based drag.
5. **Given** a board viewer, **When** they attempt to drag any card or lane, **Then** the drag is not initiated and no reordering occurs.
6. **Given** two members submit moves for the same card simultaneously, **When** both requests reach the system, **Then** exactly one succeeds and the other receives a conflict response prompting a refresh; the final board state is consistent with exactly one winner.

---

### User Story 4 - Board Owner Invites and Manages Board Members (Priority: P2)

A board owner (or system admin) invites a person to collaborate on a specific board by specifying the person's email address and the role they should have: Owner, Member, or Viewer. The system issues a single-use time-limited invitation link. When the invitee accepts, they become a registered user of the system (if they are not already one) and are immediately added to the board with the assigned role. The owner can also change a member's role or remove a member from the board after they have joined.

**Why this priority**: Collaboration is the entire point of a Kanban board — a solo board is a to-do list. But the core board experience from US1–US3 can be demonstrated solo first, making this P2.

**Independent Test**: Sign in as a board owner, issue a board invitation for a new email with the Member role. Accept the invitation with a matching Google account. Confirm the new user appears in the board's member list with the Member role and can add cards. Change their role to Viewer and confirm they can no longer add cards. Remove them from the board and confirm they no longer appear in the member list and receive a not-found response when accessing the board.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a board owner is signed in, **When** they invite `newperson@example.com` to a board with the Member role, **Then** the system records a pending board membership for that email and role and returns a redemption link the owner can share.

83	4. **Given** a board has a member, **When** the board owner changes that member's role from Member to Viewer, **Then** the member's board role is updated and they can no longer perform write operations on the board; their existing read access continues.
84	5. **Given** a board has a member, **When** the board owner removes that member, **Then** the member no longer appears in the board's member list and any subsequent request from that user to access the board returns a not-found response.

87	
88	---
89	
90	### User Story 5 - Viewer Browses a Board Read-Only (Priority: P3)
91	
92	A registered user assigned the Viewer role on a board can see the board's lanes and cards in full but cannot make any changes. This enables stakeholders to monitor progress without the risk of accidental edits.
93	
94	**Why this priority**: A pure read-only persona is valuable for reporting and oversight, but the product delivers its primary value without it — owners and members can share a board without assigning Viewer-only roles.
95	
96	**Independent Test**: Assign a user the Viewer role on a board. Sign in as that user. Confirm all lanes and cards are visible. Confirm that any attempt to create, update, delete, or move any item is refused.
97	
98	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
99	
100	1. **Given** a user has the Viewer role on a board, **When** they retrieve the board, **Then** all lanes and cards are returned in full.
101	2. **Given** a user has the Viewer role, **When** they attempt any write operation — create card, update card, delete card, create lane, rename lane, delete lane, move card, reorder lane — **Then** each request is refused with a permission-denied response.
102	
103	---
104	
105	### Edge Cases
106	
107	- **Concurrent card moves to the same position**: two members drag different cards to the same lane position simultaneously; both operations succeed but land at distinct adjacent positions — neither card is lost.
108	- **Delete a lane that contains cards**: all cards within the lane are removed along with the lane in a single atomic operation; the UI presents a destructive confirmation step before executing.

1. **Given** a board owner is signed in, **When** they invite `newperson@example.com` to a board with the Member role, **Then** the system records a pending board membership for that email and role and returns a redemption link the owner can share.
2. **Given** `newperson@example.com` has not yet registered, **When** they open the board invitation link and complete sign-in with a matching account, **Then** the system creates a registered user record for them, adds them to the board with the Member role, and presents the board they were invited to.
3. **Given** `existing@example.com` is already a registered user, **When** they open a board invitation and complete sign-in, **Then** the system adds them to the board with the specified role without creating a duplicate user record.
4. **Given** a board has a member, **When** the board owner changes that member's role from Member to Viewer, **Then** the member's board role is updated and they can no longer perform write operations on the board; their existing read access continues.
5. **Given** a board has a member, **When** the board owner removes that member, **Then** the member no longer appears in the board's member list and any subsequent request from that user to access the board returns a not-found response.
6. **Given** a registered member is the sole Owner of a board, **When** someone attempts to remove them or change their role to a non-Owner role, **Then** the system refuses with a clear message that at least one Owner must remain on the board.
7. **Given** a board Member (not Owner or Admin), **When** they attempt to invite someone, change a member's role, or remove a member, **Then** the request is refused with a permission-denied response.

---

### User Story 5 - Viewer Browses a Board Read-Only (Priority: P3)

A registered user assigned the Viewer role on a board can see the board's lanes and cards in full but cannot make any changes. This enables stakeholders to monitor progress without the risk of accidental edits.

**Why this priority**: A pure read-only persona is valuable for reporting and oversight, but the product delivers its primary value without it — owners and members can share a board without assigning Viewer-only roles.

**Independent Test**: Assign a user the Viewer role on a board. Sign in as that user. Confirm all lanes and cards are visible. Confirm that any attempt to create, update, delete, or move any item is refused.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user has the Viewer role on a board, **When** they retrieve the board, **Then** all lanes and cards are returned in full.
2. **Given** a user has the Viewer role, **When** they attempt any write operation — create card, update card, delete card, create lane, rename lane, delete lane, move card, reorder lane — **Then** each request is refused with a permission-denied response.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Concurrent card moves to the same position**: two members drag different cards to the same lane position simultaneously; both operations succeed but land at distinct adjacent positions — neither card is lost.
- **Delete a lane that contains cards**: all cards within the lane are removed along with the lane in a single atomic operation; the UI presents a destructive confirmation step before executing.
- **Reorder when only one card or lane exists**: moving the sole item in a list is a no-op that succeeds without error.
- **Board with no lanes**: retrieving such a board returns an empty lane list, not an error.
- **Card position gaps after deletion**: removing a card from the middle of a list produces a gapless position sequence; retrieval must never expose gaps.
- **Non-member accesses a board by ID**: a registered user who is not a member of the requested board receives a not-found response — never a forbidden response — to prevent board enumeration.
- **Admin access boundary**: an admin must be a board member to access board data. Creating a board automatically grants the admin the Owner board role on that board; they have no ambient access to boards they did not create or join.
- **Renaming a lane to a name that duplicates an existing lane in the same board**: the system rejects with a clear message that lane names must be unique within a board.
- **Board deletion**: only the board Owner or system Admin can delete a board; all lanes, cards, memberships, and card assignments are deleted atomically; this is permanent and the UI requires explicit confirmation.
- **Invitation to an email already on the board**: if an unconsumed, unexpired invitation already exists for that email on that board, the existing link is returned rather than a new one being issued.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

#### Board Management

- **FR-001**: System MUST allow system administrators to create boards by providing a name (1–200 characters) that is unique across all boards. On creation, the creating administrator is automatically assigned the Owner board role.
- **FR-002**: System MUST list only boards the requesting user is a member of (any role). Boards the user has no membership in MUST NOT appear in any listing.
- **FR-003**: System MUST allow board Owners and system Admins to delete a board. Deletion MUST atomically remove all lanes, cards, memberships, and card assignments associated with that board.
- **FR-004**: System MUST return a not-found response for any board resource request from a registered user who is not a member of that board — regardless of whether the board actually exists.

#### Lane Management

- **FR-005**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to create lanes within a board by providing a name (1–100 characters) that is unique within that board. A new lane is appended at the end of the current lane list.
- **FR-006**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to rename an existing lane. The new name MUST be unique within the board.
- **FR-007**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to delete a lane. Deleting a lane MUST also delete all cards it contains in a single atomic operation.
- **FR-008**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to move a lane to a new position within its board. All other lanes' positions MUST be updated so the sequence remains gapless after every reorder.
- **FR-009**: Lane positions MUST be unique within a board and MUST remain gapless (1, 2, 3, …) after every create, delete, and reorder operation.

#### Card Management

- **FR-010**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to create cards within a lane by providing a title (1–200 characters). Description (up to 2000 characters) and due date are optional at creation. A new card is appended at the bottom of the lane's card list.

141	- **FR-012**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to delete a card. The remaining cards in that lane MUST have their positions adjusted to remain gapless.
142	- **FR-013**: System MUST allow board Owners and Members to move a card to a new position within its current lane or to a different lane at a specified position. All affected card positions within both lanes MUST be updated atomically.
143	- **FR-014**: Card positions MUST be unique within a lane and MUST remain gapless after every create, move, and delete operation.

146	
147	- **FR-015**: System MUST allow board Owners and system Admins to invite a person to a board by specifying the invitee's email address and the intended board role (Owner, Member, or Viewer).
148	- **FR-016**: System MUST issue a single-use, time-limited (7-day) redemption link per board invitation. If an unconsumed, unexpired invitation for the same email on the same board already exists, the existing link MUST be returned rather than a new one being created.

164

174

176	- **SC-002**: Dragging a card between lanes reflects the new position in the UI in under 100 milliseconds from release, and the server confirms the move in under 2 seconds.
177	- **SC-003**: Dragging a lane to a new position reflects the change in the UI in under 100 milliseconds from release, and the server confirms the move in under 2 seconds.

179	- **SC-005**: When a card or lane move fails, the item returns visually to its original position with a visible persistent error message within 1 second of the failure — the user is never left with a board state that silently disagrees with the server.
180	- **SC-006**: Across 20 simultaneous move attempts on the same card, exactly one succeeds and the rest receive a conflict response. The board is in a single consistent state after all attempts resolve.
181	- **SC-007**: A keyboard-only user can move a card between lanes and reorder lanes without using a pointing device. All interactions are reachable by keyboard tab order.
182	- **SC-008**: A board viewer can load and read a board with 100 cards in under 3 seconds and cannot trigger any write operation regardless of how they interact with the UI.
183	- **SC-009**: Board invitation acceptance by a person not yet registered completes and presents the invited board in under 2 minutes from opening the link (assumes the invitee has a valid account with the identity provider).
184	- **SC-010**: Requests for a board by a non-member return a not-found response in under 200 milliseconds — board existence is never revealed to non-members.

194	- **The invitation acceptance flow from the auth spec (001-auth-onboarding) is extended for board invitations**: board invitations reuse the same token and acceptance mechanism but additionally create the board membership record on acceptance. No separate invitation infrastructure is introduced.

### User Story 6 - Unify Input Validation Using FluentValidation Across All Layers (Priority: P1)

The codebase currently maintains two separate input-validation mechanisms: FluentValidation at the API boundary (where it handles user-supplied input on incoming requests) and a bespoke `Verify` guard-clause class in the inner layers (Business, DataAccess, Domain, AntiCorruption). This duplication means two patterns to learn, two exception types to map in error-handling middleware, and two sets of test assertions to maintain. Consolidating on FluentValidation throughout removes this inconsistency and establishes a single, well-known library as the project's universal input-validation tool.

**Why this priority**: All new services introduced in US1–US5 must adopt the chosen validation pattern from day one. Completing this migration before implementing the board, lane, card, and membership services prevents the legacy pattern from spreading further and avoids a double-migration.

**Independent Test**: Call any business service method or repository method with a null, empty, or otherwise invalid argument. Confirm a `FluentValidation.ValidationException` is thrown (not `ArgumentNullException` or `ArgumentException`). Confirm that the API returns a `422 Unprocessable Entity` with a Problem Details body describing the validation failure. Confirm no reference to `Verify.cs` remains in the compiled solution.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a business service method is called with a null required argument, **When** the call is processed, **Then** a `FluentValidation.ValidationException` is thrown describing the null violation — no `ArgumentNullException` is raised.
2. **Given** a business service method is called with an empty string where a non-empty value is required, **When** the call is processed, **Then** a `FluentValidation.ValidationException` is thrown describing the empty-string violation.
3. **Given** a repository method is called with a default (empty) GUID where a valid identifier is required, **When** the call is processed, **Then** a `FluentValidation.ValidationException` is thrown describing the invalid identifier.
4. **Given** any inner-layer `ValidationException` propagates to the API, **When** the exception handler processes it, **Then** the response status is `422 Unprocessable Entity` with a Problem Details body containing a `code` field and the validation error details — no stack trace is exposed.
5. **Given** the migration is complete, **When** the solution is compiled, **Then** there are zero references to `Verify.cs`, `ParameterVerifier<T>`, or any of the `Verify` extension classes — they do not exist in the compiled output.

112	  storage is permitted.

114	  Use ASP.NET model validation (`[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`, `FluentValidation`) on every DTO.
115	- OWASP Top 10 awareness is required for all API and UI work.
116	
117	**SQL injection prevention (Dapper-specific):**
118	- ALL Dapper queries MUST use `@paramName` placeholders. String concatenation into SQL is a
119	  critical violation — even for `ORDER BY` clauses or dynamic filters.
120	- Dynamic `ORDER BY`: use a compile-time whitelist dictionary and look up the safe column name.
121	  Never interpolate user-supplied values into SQL text.
122	- Dynamic `WHERE` filters: build predicates with a parameter dictionary, never via string
123	  interpolation.
124	
125	**Secret detection — hard gate (non-negotiable):**
126	- **gitleaks** MUST be installed as a git pre-commit hook. A commit containing a detected secret
127	  MUST be blocked at the hook level. No bypass (`--no-verify`) without explicit written approval.
128	- A `.gitleaks.toml` MUST be committed to the repo root and kept current.
129	- If gitleaks is not installed, the pre-commit hook MUST refuse and print install instructions.
130	- Environment variables and secrets managers are the only permitted credential transport.
131	  Hardcoded secrets anywhere in the codebase — including test fixtures — are a critical violation.
132	
133	**Snyk (free tier — https://app.snyk.io) MUST cover the full security surface:**
134	- **SCA**: dependency vulnerability detection
135	- **SAST**: code-level security issues in C# and TypeScript
136	- **License compliance**: open source license risk flagged before merge
137	- **IaC scanning**: infrastructure-as-code files scanned if present
138	- **Container**: image scanning for base-image CVEs (required when containers are built in CI)
139	- All developers MUST have the **Snyk VS Code extension** installed and active.
140	- Snyk-flagged medium, high, or critical severity findings block merge.
141	
142	**Security headers — defense in depth (non-negotiable):**
143	- Response security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy,
144	  Permissions-Policy) MUST be applied via middleware to all responses including 404s
145	  and error responses — see *Security Headers*.
146	- Missing or weakened security headers are a Snyk SAST blocking finding.

148	### V. SOLID (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
149	Every class and interface MUST comply with all five SOLID principles:
150	
151	- **Single Responsibility**: Each class has exactly one reason to change.
152	- **Open/Closed**: Classes are open for extension, closed for modification. Extend via new types,
153	  not edits to existing ones.
154	- **Liskov Substitution**: Subtypes MUST be fully substitutable for their base types without
155	  altering correctness.
156	- **Interface Segregation**: Prefer many focused interfaces over one general-purpose interface.
157	  No client MUST depend on methods it does not use.
158	- **Dependency Inversion**: High-level modules MUST NOT depend on low-level modules. Both MUST
159	  depend on abstractions. Inject dependencies; never instantiate them inside a class.
160	
161	SOLID violations MUST be raised in code review and MUST be remediated before merge.
162	
163	### VI. Self-Documenting Code
164	Code MUST communicate intent through naming alone. Comments inside a class are a code smell.
165	
166	- Method names MUST describe exactly what the method does. If a comment is needed to explain a
167	  method body, rename the method or extract a helper until no comment is needed.
168	- Variables, parameters, and types MUST be named at the level of intent, not implementation
169	  (e.g., `pendingCardIds` not `list`, `BoardRepository` not `Repo`).
170	- If a reader would be surprised by a behavior, that behavior belongs in the name, not a comment.
171	- The only permitted comments are: (a) public API XML doc comments on REST endpoint contracts and
172	  (b) links to external specifications or RFCs that cannot be expressed in code.
173	
174	### VII. Established Design Patterns
175	All structural decisions MUST follow well-established GoF or DDD patterns. Ad-hoc structures
176	require documented justification in the plan's Complexity Tracking table.
177	
178	Required patterns by layer:
179	
180	| Layer | Required Pattern |
181	|-------|-----------------|
182	| Business layer | Fluent interface; Builders created via Factories |
183	| Domain | Aggregate roots, Value objects, Domain events |
184	| Data access | Repository pattern (Dapper against `IDbConnection`) |
185	| Anti-corruption | Adapter pattern wrapping all external API calls |
186	| REST API | Minimal API endpoint handlers; no business logic in endpoint handlers |
187	| React frontend | Container/Presentational split; custom hooks for shared logic |
188	| React components | Fluent UI 2 components; React Testing Library for component tests |
189	
190	When selecting patterns, agents MUST query the Microsoft Learn MCP server for current best
191	practices for C# and React before proposing an implementation approach.
192	
193	### VIII. MVP-Oriented Delivery
194	Every feature decision MUST be evaluated against the question: *does this move us toward a
195	product that users love?*
196	
197	The SVPG definition of MVP governs: **MVP means minimum scope, not minimum quality.** An MVP
198	is the smallest set of features that delivers genuine value — something users actively choose
199	over alternatives, not merely tolerate. A low-quality, barely-functional release is not an MVP;
200	it is a prototype, and MUST NOT be shipped as a product.
201	
202	- Every spec MUST identify which user problem is being solved and for whom.
203	- Features MUST be prioritized by user value, not engineering convenience.
204	- "Minimum" applies to scope; quality, usability, and performance standards are
205	  non-negotiable even in the first shipped increment.
206	- Agents and developers MUST challenge features that add scope without proportional user value.
207	
208	### IX. Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)
209	NFRs are first-class acceptance criteria on every feature. A feature that passes functional
210	tests but fails NFR gates is not complete.
211	
212	#### Maintainability
213	- SOLID compliance and self-documenting code (see Principles V and VI) are the primary
214	  maintainability gates.
215	- Cyclomatic complexity per method MUST stay ≤ 10.
216	- Every public interface in `Kanban.Business` and `Kanban.Domain` MUST have an xUnit test
217	  exercising its contract so regressions are caught immediately.
218	- Agents MUST prefer extending existing abstractions over introducing new ones.
219	
220	#### Usability
221	- All UI MUST be built with **Microsoft Fluent UI 2** (`@fluentui/react-components`).
222	  No custom component framework.
223	- All interactive components MUST meet **WCAG 2.1 AA** accessibility standards.
224	- Fluent UI 2 accessibility props (`aria-*`, keyboard navigation, focus management) MUST be
225	  used correctly on every component.
226	- User flows MUST be validated by Playwright e2e tests that exercise keyboard-only navigation.
227	- Component tests MUST use React Testing Library's accessibility queries
228	  (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) over implementation-detail selectors (`getByTestId`).
229	
230	- **Fluent UI ARIA contract (non-negotiable):**
231	  - Typography components (`Title1`, `Title2`, `Body1`, etc.) render as `<span>` by default.
232	    When they serve as a page or section heading, they MUST use the `as="h1"` (or appropriate
233	    level) prop so that `getByRole('heading', { level: N })` locators work. Missing `as` props
234	    are both an a11y defect and a test-locator defect.
235	  - `MessageBar` renders as `role="group"` by default. Any `MessageBar` conveying a transient
236	    status or error MUST add `role="alert"` explicitly so it participates in the ARIA live
237	    region tree and is reachable via `getByRole('alert')`.
238	  - Every RTL component test for a page MUST assert `getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })` as
239	    an explicit WCAG AA gate. A page without a level-1 heading fails the accessibility audit.
240	
241	#### Performance
242	- React component re-renders MUST be profiled; unnecessary re-renders MUST be eliminated
243	  before a feature is merged (use `React.memo`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` where measured).
244	- REST API response time MUST be ≤ 200ms at the 95th percentile for all read operations under
245	  normal load.
246	- Frontend initial bundle size MUST be monitored; new dependencies require bundle impact
247	  justification before merge.
248	- Database queries MUST use parameterized Dapper calls; N+1 queries are a blocking defect.

307	These are the governing concepts for `Kanban.Domain`. The SQL schema lives in the feature spec

311	|--------|-------------|
312	| **User** | Authenticated via Google OAuth; has identity, display name, avatar, and SystemRole |
313	| **Board** | Top-level container; owned by a User; has members with roles (owner/member/viewer) |

328	## Authorization Model
329	
330	### Three-Layer Access Model
331	
332	1. **Google OAuth** — proves identity (valid token = authenticated)
333	2. **`RegisteredUser` policy** — proves the authenticated Google user has an active record in
334	   the `users` table (invited and accepted)
335	3. **`BoardMembershipRequirement`** — proves the registered user has the required role on the
336	   specific board being accessed
337	
338	### Two-Level Role Model
339	
340	- **System roles** (`User.SystemRole`): `Admin`, `Standard` — stored on the `User` entity
341	- **Board roles** (`board_members.Role`): `Owner`, `Member`, `Viewer` — stored per membership
342	
343	### Operation Matrix
344	
345	| Operation | Admin | Owner | Member | Viewer |
346	|-----------|-------|-------|--------|--------|
347	| Create board | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
348	| Send invites | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
349	| Read board / lanes / cards | ✓* | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
350	| Create / update / delete cards and lanes | ✓* | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
351	| Manage members | ✓* | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
352	| Delete board | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
353	
354	*Admin must be a board member to access board data. Creating a board automatically grants
355	Admin the Owner board role on that board. There is no ambient super-access to all boards.
356	
357	### Authorization Policies
358	
359	```csharp
360	builder.Services.AddAuthorizationBuilder()
361	    .AddPolicy("RegisteredUser", policy => policy
362	        .RequireAuthenticatedUser()
363	        .AddRequirements(new RegisteredUserRequirement()))
364	    .AddPolicy("Admin", policy => policy
365	        .RequireAuthenticatedUser()
366	        .RequireClaim("system_role", "admin"));
367	```
368	
369	`RegisteredUserHandler` checks that the `sub` claim maps to an active `User` record in the DB.
370	Unregistered Google users receive `403` with Problem Details `code: "user.not_registered"` —
371	never `401` (they ARE authenticated, just not registered).
372	
373	### System Role Claim Flow
374	
375	The `system_role` claim is added during the OIDC `OnTicketReceived` callback after the `User`
376	record is resolved from the DB — stored in the auth session. No DB lookup on subsequent requests.
377	
378	### Endpoint Authorization Structure
379	
380	- `POST /api/v1/boards` — requires `Admin` policy
381	- `POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/accept` — requires `RequireAuthorization()` only
382	  (Google auth, not `RegisteredUser` — invitee is not yet registered)
383	- All other endpoints — require `RegisteredUser` policy via versioned endpoint group
384	
385	### Invite Flow
386	
387	1. Board owner or Admin sends invite (email + board + role) → creates `pending` `board_members`
388	   record
389	2. Invitee receives email with a single-use token expiring in 7 days
390	3. Invitee clicks link → Google OAuth → `POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/accept`
391	4. Accept endpoint: creates `User` record if absent, activates `board_members` record, marks
392	   token consumed
393	
394	### Enumeration Prevention
395	
396	Boards the requesting user is not a member of MUST return `404` — even if they exist.
397	`403` is only returned for operations on a board the user can see but lacks the role for.
398	
399	### Resource-Based Authorization Implementation
400	
401	- `BoardOperations` static class: `Read`, `CreateCard`, `UpdateCard`, `DeleteCard`,
402	  `CreateLane`, `UpdateLane`, `DeleteLane`, `ManageMembers`, `DeleteBoard`
403	- `BoardMembershipRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement`
404	- `BoardAuthorizationHandler : AuthorizationHandler<BoardMembershipRequirement, BoardContext>`
405	- `BoardContext` — lightweight value type `{ BoardId, ResolvedRole }` loaded once per request
406	- Enforcement: Business layer service methods call `IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync` —
407	  never in endpoint handlers
408	- Identity flow: `IHttpContextAccessor` → scoped `ICurrentUserService` resolves
409	  `User.ExternalId` from Google `sub` claim → injected into Business layer (same DI seam
410	  where `TenantContext` slots in for multi-tenancy)
411	
412	### Initial Admin Seeding
413	
414	The initial Admin `User` record is created in a DbUp seed migration. The email is configured
415	via the `Seed:AdminEmail` user secret — never hardcoded. On first Google login with that email
416	the OIDC callback matches the `email` claim to the seeded record and writes the `sub` claim
417	back, linking the Google identity permanently. Subsequent logins use `sub` only.

421	## Transaction Pattern
422	
423	> Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/data/sqlite/transactions
424	
425	SQLite allows only **one write transaction at a time**. Transactions are serializable by default.
426	All transaction handling MUST follow the patterns below, informed by the Microsoft Learn SQLite
427	transactions documentation.
428	
429	### Standard pattern — deferred transaction
430	
431	Use `BeginTransaction(deferred: true)` for any operation that reads before writing. A deferred
432	transaction starts as a read and upgrades to a write only when the first write executes,
433	maximising concurrent read access during the read phase.
434	
435	```csharp
436	using var transaction = connection.BeginTransaction(deferred: true);
437	try
438	{
439	    // All Dapper calls must receive the transaction explicitly
440	    transaction.Commit();
441	}
442	catch
443	{
444	    transaction.Rollback();
445	    throw;
446	}
447	```
448	
449	**Retry with Polly**: a deferred transaction that attempts to upgrade from read to write while
450	the database is locked will throw. The Business layer MUST use **Polly** to wrap deferred write
451	operations with a retry policy (2–3 attempts, exponential backoff) before surfacing the error.
452	Polly is the standard resilience mechanism for all transient failures across the application —
453	database lock contention, external API timeouts, and any other retriable fault.
454	
455	### Optimistic concurrency — savepoints
456	
457	For concurrent update scenarios (e.g. two users moving the same card), use savepoints:
458	
459	```csharp
460	using var transaction = connection.BeginTransaction();
461	var updated = false;
462	do
463	{
464	    transaction.Save("optimistic-update");
465	    var rowsAffected = /* Dapper UPDATE with version/timestamp check */;
466	    if (rowsAffected == 0)
467	    {
468	        transaction.Rollback("optimistic-update");
469	        // resolve conflict, then retry within the same outer transaction
470	    }
471	    else
472	    {
473	        transaction.Release("optimistic-update");
474	        updated = true;
475	    }
476	} while (!updated);
477	transaction.Commit();
478	```
479	
480	### Rules
481	- **No `TransactionScope`** — use `IDbTransaction` directly. `TransactionScope` promotes to DTC,
482	  which SQLite does not support.
483	- Every Dapper call inside a transaction MUST receive the `IDbTransaction` instance explicitly.
484	- **No external API calls, I/O, or network operations inside a transaction.** Acquire all
485	  external data before opening the transaction. See *HTTP Resilience* for the outbound
486	  HTTP pattern — outbound calls MUST happen before `BeginTransaction()`.
487	- Transactions MUST be kept as short as possible — open late, commit early.
488	- This pattern is portable to PostgreSQL: deferred transactions and savepoints are supported
489	  in Npgsql with equivalent semantics.

494	
495	SQLite is used for local development (zero config, file-based). The architecture MUST make

506	  that works in both engines.
507	- All CI integration tests run against SQLite. Postgres-specific behavior is validated in a

514	## Multi-Tenancy Readiness
515	
516	Multi-tenancy is **out of scope for MVP**. However, the architecture MUST make it achievable
517	via targeted migration — not a rewrite. The following seam decisions are made now, mirroring
518	the approach taken for database portability.
519	
520	- **All data access is user-scoped from day one.** No repository method returns data without a
521	  `userId` or equivalent principal in scope. There are no "list everything" queries that would
522	  accidentally cross tenant boundaries. Adding `tenantId` alongside `userId` later is additive.
523	- **Authentication context flows through DI, not method parameters.** The authenticated user's
524	  identity is resolved from a scoped service (claims from `IHttpContextAccessor`). This is the
525	  same seam where a `TenantContext` would later be inserted — one registration change, not a
526	  parameter-chain refactor across every method signature.
527	- **Board is already the natural tenant boundary.** The Board membership model (owner + members
528	  with roles) resembles an org-scoped access model. When multi-tenancy is introduced, an
529	  `Organization` aggregate wrapping Boards is the expected migration path.
530	- **GUIDs for all primary keys.** GUID-keyed entities are tenant-portable and safe for
531	  cross-shard or cross-database routing without collisions.
532	- **No static or ambient application state.** All services are DI-registered as scoped or
533	  transient. A scoped `TenantContext` can be added and injected into any repository or business
534	  service without architectural surgery.
535	- **`IDbConnection` abstraction** also enables database-per-tenant routing: the connection
536	  factory can resolve the correct connection string by tenant ID without any repository changes.
537	
538	When multi-tenancy is introduced, the migration path is:
539	1. Add `Organization` aggregate and `tenant_id` to `boards` (cascade as needed).
540	2. Register a scoped `TenantContext` resolved from the auth token.
541	3. Inject `TenantContext` into repositories alongside the existing user context.
542	4. Update the connection factory if database-per-tenant isolation is required.

546	## Containerization Readiness
547	
548	Production deployment is expected to be containerized. The architecture MUST make this a
549	deployment-time decision, not a code change. The following seams are decided now to mirror
550	the approach taken for *Database Portability* and *Multi-Tenancy Readiness*.
551	
552	### Core Principles
553	
554	- **Stateless API.** No static or ambient state. No in-memory session, no in-memory cache
555	  for cross-request data. All services DI-registered as scoped or transient (already enforced
556	  by Principle V and the multi-tenancy seam — reinforced here for containers). Any future
557	  caching MUST go through `IDistributedCache` so the implementation can swap from in-memory
558	  (single replica) to Redis (multi-replica) at registration time without code changes.
559	- **Configuration via environment variables.** No file-based secrets in containers. User
560	  secrets are a local-dev-only mechanism; production reads configuration exclusively from
561	  environment variables or a secrets manager via `IConfiguration` providers
562	  (see *Local Secrets Management* and *Configuration & Options Pattern*).
563	- **Logs to stdout only.** No file-based log providers (`AddFile()` is forbidden). The
564	  orchestrator collects stdout/stderr. `AddJsonConsole()` is the production output (already
565	  mandated in *Structured Logging*).
566	- **Idempotent, fast startup.** Migrations run on application startup but MUST be safe under
567	  concurrent replica boot — see *Health & Lifecycle — Migration Coordination*.
568	
569	### Image Strategy
570	
571	| Concern | Decision |
572	|---------|----------|
573	| Runtime base | `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled` — Microsoft-recommended distroless-style image for .NET 10; ~30MB, non-root by default |
574	| Build base | `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` — multi-stage build, final image contains only runtime + published output |
575	| User | Non-root (chiseled image's built-in `app` user) |
576	| Exposed port | 8080 (chiseled default — no root required) |
577	| Frontend image | Separate static container in production (CDN-friendly, scale-independent). Local dev continues to use Vite dev server. |

579	### `.dockerignore`
580	
581	MUST be committed to the repo root alongside the eventual Dockerfile. MUST exclude at minimum:
582	
583	```
584	**/bin/
585	**/obj/
586	**/node_modules/
587	.git/
588	.vs/
589	.vscode/
590	tests/
591	*.user
592	*.suo

597	The user-secrets store (`~/.microsoft/usersecrets/`) is outside the build context, but

600	### Image Scanning
601	
602	- **Snyk Container** MUST run in CI on every published image. Medium/high/critical findings
603	  block merge — same gate as SCA and SAST (Principle IV).
604	- Images MUST be published with an immutable tag (`sha-<commit>`) plus a mutable `latest`
605	  tag. Production deploys MUST reference the immutable tag.
606	
607	### SQLite in Containers — Caveat
608	
609	SQLite is the local-dev DB. In a containerized deploy SQLite requires a mounted volume and
610	is incompatible with multi-replica deploys (single-writer constraint, no shared filesystem).
611	**The recommended container deploy path is Postgres** — already supported by the
612	`IDbConnection` seam (see *Database Portability*). Single-replica SQLite deploys with a
613	mounted volume are technically supported but should be reserved for demo / single-tenant
614	pilot scenarios.
615	
616	### Forwarded Headers — Mandatory When Behind Ingress
617	
618	When the API runs behind ingress / load balancer (the default container deploy topology),
619	`UseForwardedHeaders` MUST be the FIRST middleware — before `UseRouting`. Without it OIDC
620	redirects break (scheme appears as `http` not `https`) and client IP logging is wrong.
621	
622	```csharp
623	app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions {
624	    ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto
625	});
626	app.UseRouting();
627	app.UseCors("KanbanWebApp");
628	app.UseAuthentication();
629	app.UseAuthorization();
630	```
631	
632	`KnownNetworks` / `KnownProxies` MUST be configured for the production ingress range —
633	accepting forwarded headers from arbitrary upstreams is a spoofing vector.

637	## Health & Lifecycle
638	
639	Container orchestrators (Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps, ECS) require liveness and
640	readiness probes to perform rolling deploys without dropping requests. These endpoints are
641	mandatory regardless of whether the MVP is containerized — they are zero-cost to add now
642	and standard infrastructure when needed.
643	
644	### Health Check Endpoints
645	
646	```csharp
647	builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
648	    .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy(), tags: ["live"])
649	    .AddCheck<DatabaseHealthCheck>("database", tags: ["ready"]);
650	
651	app.MapHealthChecks("/health/live", new HealthCheckOptions {
652	    Predicate = check => check.Tags.Contains("live")
653	});
654	app.MapHealthChecks("/health/ready", new HealthCheckOptions {
655	    Predicate = check => check.Tags.Contains("ready")
656	});
657	```
658	
659	| Endpoint | What it checks | Auth |
660	|---------|----------------|------|
661	| `/health/live` | Process is responsive — does NOT touch DB or any dependency | None |
662	| `/health/ready` | All dependencies (DB connectivity) are healthy | None |
663	
664	**Rules (non-negotiable):**
665	
666	- Liveness MUST NOT touch the database. A slow query MUST NOT cause the orchestrator to
667	  kill the container.
668	- Readiness MUST verify DB connectivity via a lightweight query (`SELECT 1`).
669	- Neither endpoint requires authentication — orchestrator probes do not carry tokens.
670	- Both endpoints MUST be excluded from request logging — they fire every few seconds and
671	  would drown the log stream.
672	
673	### Graceful Shutdown
674	
675	```csharp
676	builder.Services.Configure<HostOptions>(opts => {
677	    opts.ShutdownTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
678	});
679	```
680	
681	- On SIGTERM, ASP.NET stops accepting new requests and waits up to `ShutdownTimeout` for
682	  in-flight requests to complete.
683	- Long-running background work MUST observe `IHostApplicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping`
684	  and cancel cooperatively.
685	- Database connections are disposed via DI scope disposal — no manual cleanup required.
686	
687	### Migration Coordination on Multi-Replica Startup
688	
689	When multiple replicas start simultaneously they all attempt DbUp migrations. The DbUp
690	`SchemaVersions` journal table provides the lock naturally — DbUp begins a transaction,
691	reads the journal, and only one replica's transaction will succeed in adding a new entry.
692	Losing replicas observe the migration already applied and proceed.
693	
694	**No explicit init container or one-shot job is required for MVP.** If a future migration
695	is destructive or long-running, that specific migration MUST be promoted to a one-shot job
696	pattern — but the default path stays in-process.

700	## Error Handling
701	
702	### Backend — Three-Layer Setup in `Program.cs`
703	
704	```csharp
705	builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
706	builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<DomainExceptionHandler>();
707	builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<InfrastructureExceptionHandler>();
708	builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<FallbackExceptionHandler>();
709	
710	app.UseExceptionHandler();      // activates the IExceptionHandler chain
711	app.UseStatusCodePages();       // ensures 4xx/5xx without a body get RFC 7807 bodies
712	```
713	
714	- `DeveloperExceptionPage` is enabled by default in Development — full stack trace visible.
715	  It MUST NEVER be active in production.
716	- Every error response MUST include a `traceId` field (`Activity.Current?.Id`) for correlation.
717	- Production responses MUST NEVER contain: stack traces, exception class names, SQL text,
718	  file paths, or internal IDs.
719	
720	### Custom Exception Hierarchy
721	
722	Exceptions live in `Kanban.Domain` (domain rules) and `Kanban.Business` (application-level).
723	They have no knowledge of HTTP — status code mapping happens exclusively in middleware.
724	
725	```
726	KanbanException (abstract base)
727	├── DomainException (abstract)
728	│   ├── NotFoundException           → 404
729	│   ├── ForbiddenException          → 404 (board enumeration) or 403 (known-board operation)
730	│   ├── ConflictException           → 409 (optimistic concurrency, duplicate names)
731	│   └── BusinessRuleException       → 422 (business rule violations)
732	└── InfrastructureException (abstract)
733	    ├── DataAccessException         → 500 (DB failure after Polly exhausted)
734	    └── ExternalServiceException    → 502 (Google OAuth, ACL failures)
735	```
736	
737	Each exception carries a `Code` string (e.g. `"board.not_found"`) surfaced in the Problem
738	Details `code` extension field for typed frontend error handling.
739	
740	### IExceptionHandler Chain
741	
742	- **`DomainExceptionHandler`** — maps `DomainException` hierarchy to status codes; writes
743	  Problem Details with `code` and `traceId`
744	- **`InfrastructureExceptionHandler`** — maps `InfrastructureException` hierarchy
745	- **`FallbackExceptionHandler`** — logs the full exception at `Error` level internally;
746	  returns ONLY `{ title: "An unexpected error occurred", traceId: "..." }` to the client —
747	  no `detail`, no stack trace, no internal names
748	
749	### Parameter Verification — Fluent `Verify` Class
750	
751	Lives in `Kanban.Domain` (no dependencies; accessible to all layers).
752	
753	**Rule:** ALL public method parameters that are non-nullable and non-optional MUST be verified
754	as the very first statements in the method body. Nullable (`string?`, `Guid?`) and optional
755	(default value) parameters are exempt.
756	
757	```csharp
758	// Static entry point — CallerArgumentExpression captures param name automatically
759	public static class Verify
760	{
761	    public static ParameterVerifier<T> That<T>(
762	        T value,
763	        [CallerArgumentExpression(nameof(value))] string paramName = "")
764	        => new(value, paramName);
765	}
766	
767	// Usage — no nameof() required
768	public Card CreateCard(string title, Guid laneId, int position, string? description)
769	{
770	    Verify.That(title).IsNotNull().IsNotEmpty().HasMaxLength(200);
771	    Verify.That(laneId).IsNotDefault();
772	    Verify.That(position).IsNonNegative();
773	    // description is nullable — exempt
774	}
775	```
776	
777	**`ParameterVerifier<T>` core methods:** `IsNotNull()` → `ArgumentNullException`,
778	`IsNotDefault()` → `ArgumentException` (catches `Guid.Empty`, `0`, `false`, etc.)
779	
780	**Type-specific extension methods (generic constraints):**
781	
782	| Extension | Constraint | Checks |
783	|-----------|-----------|--------|
784	| `IsNotEmpty()` | `ParameterVerifier<string>` | non-empty string |
785	| `HasMaxLength(int)` | `ParameterVerifier<string>` | length ≤ max |
786	| `IsNotEmpty<T>()` | `IEnumerable<T>` | non-empty collection |
787	| `IsPositive<T>()` | `INumber<T>` (.NET 10) | value > 0 |
788	| `IsNonNegative<T>()` | `INumber<T>` (.NET 10) | value ≥ 0 |
789	| `IsGreaterThan<T>(T)` | `IComparable<T>` | value > threshold |
790	| `IsInRange<T>(T, T)` | `IComparable<T>` | min ≤ value ≤ max |
791	
792	`Verify` throws `ArgumentNullException` / `ArgumentException` — programming errors that map
793	to `500` via `FallbackExceptionHandler`. If `Verify` fires in production, a layer boundary
794	failed to validate before calling. `FluentValidation` on DTOs catches user-input problems
795	before they ever reach a `Verify` call.
796	
797	**Scope:**
798	
799	| Layer | Required? |
800	|-------|-----------|
801	| `Kanban.Business` services | Yes |
802	| `Kanban.DataAccess` repositories | Yes |
803	| `Kanban.Domain` entity / value object constructors and methods | Yes |
804	| `Kanban.AntiCorruption` adapters | Yes |
805	| `Kanban.Api` endpoint handlers | No — `FluentValidation` handles the API boundary |
806	
807	### Frontend Error Handling
808	
809	**Retry policy:** TanStack Query retries `5xx` / network errors up to 2 times with exponential
810	backoff. `4xx` responses are NEVER retried — they are deterministic failures.
811	
812	**Reconnection:** TanStack Query's `onlineManager` handles browser offline/online transitions
813	automatically — stale queries re-fetch on reconnect without custom code.
814	
815	**Failed mutations:** MUST show a persistent (non-auto-dismissing) Fluent UI toast with a
816	"Try again" action. The user is never silently left with stale state.
817	
818	**Error boundaries** — three levels using `react-error-boundary`:
819	
820	| Boundary | Scope | Fallback |
821	|----------|-------|---------|
822	| `BoardPageErrorBoundary` | Entire board page | Full-page error with retry |
823	| `LaneErrorBoundary` | Single lane | Inline lane error; other lanes unaffected |
824	| `CardErrorBoundary` | Single card | Card placeholder; lane unaffected |
825	
826	Error boundaries are NEVER placed at the app root — a single broken card MUST NOT take down
827	the board.
828	
829	### Data Loss Prevention (Non-Negotiable)
830	
831	1. **Distinguish empty from failed**: `null` / `undefined` where data is expected triggers the
832	   error boundary — never renders as an empty state. An empty board (0 lanes returned) is valid;
833	   a `null` lanes array is an error.
834	2. **Preserve drafts on mutation failure**: when a save mutation fails the form MUST restore the
835	   user's in-progress edit — the draft is never discarded on API error.
836	3. **Optimistic rollback is visible**: when a card move fails the card visually returns to its
837	   origin position AND a toast explains why — the user is never left with a board that silently
838	   disagrees with the server.
839	4. **Conflict must not silently succeed**: `ConflictException` (409) MUST surface as
840	   "This item was modified by someone else — please refresh" — never silently overwrite.
841	5. **Partial response = error**: if an API response omits required fields the frontend treats
842	   this as a failed response and triggers the appropriate error boundary — never renders a false
843	   empty state that could mislead the user into thinking data is gone.

846	
847	## Frontend State Management
848	
849	**TanStack Query v5** is the mandatory server state management solution.
850	No Redux, Zustand, or Jotai for MVP.
851	
852	### Setup
853	
854	- Packages: `@tanstack/react-query`, `@tanstack/react-query-devtools` (dev only)
855	- `QueryClient` at app root: `staleTime: 30_000`; retry policy retries `5xx` / network errors
856	  up to 2 times — NEVER retries `4xx`
857	- `QueryClientProvider` wraps `<App />`
858	- `ReactQueryDevtools` rendered in development builds only
859	
860	### Query Key Convention
861	
862	Hierarchical arrays enable precise cache invalidation:
863	
864	```
865	['boards']                                    — board list
866	['boards', boardId]                           — single board
867	['boards', boardId, 'lanes']                  — lanes for a board
868	['boards', boardId, 'lanes', laneId, 'cards'] — cards in a lane
869	```
870	
871	### Custom Hook Layer
872	
873	Components MUST NOT use `useQuery` / `useMutation` directly. All data access goes through
874	named custom hooks in `src/hooks/`:
875	
876	- **Read hooks**: `useBoards()`, `useBoard(id)`, `useLanes(boardId)`, `useCards(laneId)`
877	- **Mutation hooks**: one hook per mutation — `useCreateBoard()`, `useUpdateCard()`,
878	  `useMoveCard()`, `useDeleteLane()`, etc.
879	
880	This is where the Container/Presentational split is achieved — components import hooks, not
881	raw TanStack Query primitives.
882	
883	### Mutation Pattern
884	
885	```
886	onMutate  → optimistic cache update; snapshot previous cache state
887	onError   → rollback to snapshot + persistent toast with "Try again"
888	onSettled → invalidateQueries to sync authoritative server state
889	```
890	
891	### State Split Rule
892	
893	- **Server state** (anything persisted in the DB) → TanStack Query exclusively
894	- **UI state** (modal open/close, drag in progress, dirty form drafts) → `useState` /
895	  `useReducer` or a small `useContext`
896	
897	### Testing
898	
899	RTL tests use a `createQueryClientWrapper()` test utility providing a fresh `QueryClient`.
900	Mocks target the fetch layer (msw) — not TanStack Query internals.
901	
902	### StrictMode and One-Shot Mutations
903	
904	React 18 StrictMode intentionally double-invokes effects (mount → simulated unmount → remount)
905	in development to surface side-effect bugs. Two rules govern any component that auto-fires a
906	mutation on mount:
907	
908	**Rule 1 — Guard with `useRef`:**
909	
910	Any `useEffect` that triggers a one-shot operation (a mutation that should fire exactly once)
911	MUST use a `useRef(false)` guard. `useRef` survives StrictMode's simulated unmount; mutation
912	state and TanStack Query `MutationObserver`s do not.
913	
914	```tsx
915	const hasAttempted = useRef(false)
916	useEffect(() => {
917	  if (hasAttempted.current) return
918	  if (conditionMet) {
919	    hasAttempted.current = true
920	    // fire the one-shot operation here
921	  }
922	}, [conditionMet])
923	```
924	
925	**Rule 2 — Use `mutateAsync` when chaining imperative logic:**
926	
927	When a mutation's result drives navigation, a cascade, or any imperative follow-up action,
928	use `mutateAsync` not `mutate`:
929	
930	```tsx
931	// ✅ Promise chain survives StrictMode remount
932	mutateAsync(payload).then(() => navigate('/')).catch(() => {})
933	
934	// ❌ useEffect watching data never fires — MutationObserver is destroyed on remount
935	mutate(payload)
936	useEffect(() => { if (data) navigate('/') }, [data, navigate])
937	```
938	
939	`mutateAsync` returns a Promise whose `.then()` callbacks fire when the Promise resolves,
940	regardless of component remount. `navigate` from `useNavigate()` is a stable reference in
941	React Router v6 and is safe to call outside the render cycle.
942	
943	Use `mutate` (not `mutateAsync`) only for fire-and-forget mutations where the UI reads
944	`data` / `error` declaratively on the next render cycle.

948	## Drag and Drop
949	
950	**Packages:** `@dnd-kit/core`, `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `@dnd-kit/utilities`
951	
952	### Sensors
953	
954	`PointerSensor` + `KeyboardSensor` only. `MouseSensor` is explicitly excluded — it is less
955	accessible and redundant with `PointerSensor`. Keyboard drag-and-drop is required for
956	WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.
957	
958	### Component Structure
959	
960	```
961	<DndContext sensors onDragEnd onDragStart onDragOver>
962	  <SortableContext items={laneIds} strategy={horizontalListSortingStrategy}>
963	    {lanes.map(lane =>
964	      <LaneErrorBoundary>
965	        <SortableContext items={cardIds} strategy={verticalListSortingStrategy}>
966	          {cards.map(card => <SortableCard />)}
967	        </SortableContext>
968	      </LaneErrorBoundary>
969	    )}
970	  </SortableContext>
971	  <DragOverlay>
972	    {activeItem && <CardDragPreview card={activeItem} />}
973	  </DragOverlay>
974	</DndContext>
975	```
976	
977	`DragOverlay` renders at root level — avoids stacking context conflicts with Fluent UI portals.
978	
979	### Move Cases in `onDragEnd`
980	
981	- **Same lane**: reorder within the lane's card array by index
982	- **Different lane**: splice out of source lane, insert at target position in destination lane
983	
984	### Optimistic Update Flow (via TanStack Query)
985	
986	```
987	onDragEnd   → fire useMoveCard({ cardId, targetLaneId, newPosition })
988	onMutate    → snapshot current cache; apply optimistic reorder immediately
989	onError     → restore snapshot; card visually returns to origin + persistent toast
990	onSettled   → invalidateQueries(['boards', boardId]) — server positions become authoritative
991	```
992	
993	### Accessibility (WCAG AA Gate)
994	
995	- `announcements` prop on `DndContext`: "Picked up card X", "Moved to lane Y position Z",
996	  "Drop cancelled"
997	- `aria-describedby` on each draggable card pointing to a visually hidden instructions element
998	- Focus returns to the moved card after a successful drop
999	- Keyboard: Space to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel

1003	## CORS Configuration
1004	
1005	Named policy `"KanbanWebApp"` applied globally. No per-endpoint decoration needed.
1006	
1007	### Policy
1008	
1009	```csharp
1010	builder.Services.AddCors(options => options.AddPolicy("KanbanWebApp", policy =>
1011	    policy
1012	        .WithOrigins(builder.Configuration
1013	            .GetSection("Cors:AllowedOrigins").Get<string[]>()!)
1014	        .WithMethods("GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS")
1015	        .AllowAnyHeader()
1016	        .WithExposedHeaders("X-Correlation-Id", "api-supported-versions")));
1017	```
1018	
1019	### Origins — Environment-Driven, Never Hardcoded
1020	
1021	```json
1022	// appsettings.Development.json
1023	"Cors": { "AllowedOrigins": ["http://localhost:5173"] }
1024	// Production: environment variable Cors__AllowedOrigins__0
1025	```
1026	
1027	`AllowCredentials()` is NOT used — JWTs are sent in the `Authorization` header, not cookies.
1028	Adding it without a specific need introduces CSRF risk with no benefit.
1029	
1030	### Mandatory Middleware Order
1031	
1032	```csharp
1033	app.UseRouting();
1034	app.UseCors("KanbanWebApp");      // MUST be before authentication
1035	app.UseAuthentication();
1036	app.UseAuthorization();
1037	```
1038	
1039	Wrong middleware order silently breaks authentication. This order is non-negotiable.
1040	
1041	When the API runs behind ingress (the default containerized topology), `UseForwardedHeaders`
1042	MUST be added BEFORE `UseRouting` — see *Containerization Readiness — Forwarded Headers*.
1043	The CORS position relative to authentication is unchanged.
1044	
1045	### Hard Prohibitions (Snyk SAST Enforced)
1046	
1047	- `AllowAnyOrigin()` is **forbidden**
1048	- `AllowAnyOrigin()` + `AllowCredentials()` is a **critical violation**
1049	
1050	### Google OAuth Redirect
1051	
1052	The OIDC middleware handles the `/signin-google` callback server-side — CORS does not apply
1053	to the auth redirect URI. No special CORS carve-out is needed for authentication.

1057	## API Versioning
1058	
1059	**Package:** `Asp.Versioning.Http` — Microsoft-maintained versioning library for minimal APIs.
1060	
1061	**Strategy: URL path segment** — `/api/v1/boards`. Clearest for humans, most cacheable, best
1062	tooling support, and directly importable into Azure API Management as distinct API versions.
1063	
1064	### Setup
1065	
1066	```csharp
1067	builder.Services.AddApiVersioning(options =>
1068	{
1069	    options.DefaultApiVersion = new ApiVersion(1, 0);
1070	    options.AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified = true;
1071	    options.ReportApiVersions = true; // adds api-supported-versions response header
1072	});
1073	```

1076	
1077	```csharp
1078	var v1 = app.NewVersionedApi();
1079	var v1Group = v1.MapGroup("/api/v1")
1080	               .HasApiVersion(1, 0)
1081	               .RequireAuthorization("RegisteredUser");

1085	
1086	- All endpoints MUST be declared as v1.0 explicitly. Adding v2 is a new route group —

1088	- When v2 ships, mark v1 as deprecated — the `api-deprecated-versions` response header signals
1089	  clients to migrate. v1 MUST remain live for a defined sunset window.
1090	- Each version produces its own OpenAPI document (`/openapi/v1.json`, `/openapi/v2.json`).

1150	## Logging & Observability
1151	
1152	Logs, traces, and metrics MUST be treated as one observability surface — emitted via
1153	OpenTelemetry and exported over OTLP. `ILogger<T>` remains the in-code API for logs;
1154	OpenTelemetry is the exporter layer that ships logs, traces, and metrics out of the
1155	process together.
1156	
1157	**Library:** Built-in `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` / `ILogger<T>` for the in-code logging
1158	API. No Serilog for MVP (YAGNI — built-in structured logging covers all requirements).
1159	OpenTelemetry SDK + OTLP exporter for shipping signals out.
1160	
1161	### Injection Scope
1162	
1163	`ILogger<T>` injected via constructor in `Kanban.Business` and `Kanban.Api` only.
1164	`Kanban.Domain` has no logging — domain logic is pure.
1165	
1166	### Structured Templates
1167	
1168	String interpolation is **forbidden** in log messages:
1169	
1170	```csharp
1171	// Correct — structured, indexed, no allocations
1172	_logger.LogInformation("Board {BoardId} retrieved for user {UserId}", boardId, userId);
1173	
1174	// Forbidden — defeats structured logging and allocates unnecessarily
1175	_logger.LogInformation($"Board {boardId} retrieved for user {userId}");
1176	```
1177	
1178	### Log Level Policy
1179	
1180	| Level | What goes here |
1181	|-------|---------------|
1182	| Debug | Query parameters, SQL text (dev only — disabled in production) |
1183	| Information | Successful CRUD, auth events (login, logout, invite accepted) |
1184	| Warning | 401/403 events, validation failures, Polly retries, slow queries >100ms |
1185	| Error | Unhandled exceptions, DB failures after Polly exhausted, OAuth errors |
1186	| Critical | Application startup failure |
1187	
1188	### PII and Sensitive Data (Non-Negotiable)
1189	
1190	- **NEVER log**: email addresses, OAuth tokens, connection strings, card content, user display
1191	  names
1192	- **Safe to log**: GUIDs (`boardId`, `userId`, `cardId`), HTTP status codes, durations,
1193	  system role
1194	
1195	### Correlation ID Middleware
1196	
1197	Every inbound request MUST be assigned a correlation ID for end-to-end tracing across
1198	services and frontend logs.
1199	
1200	```csharp
1201	app.Use(async (ctx, next) => {
1202	    var correlationId = ctx.Request.Headers["X-Correlation-Id"].FirstOrDefault()
1203	                      ?? Activity.Current?.Id
1204	                      ?? Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
1205	    Activity.Current?.SetTag("correlation.id", correlationId);
1206	    ctx.Response.Headers["X-Correlation-Id"] = correlationId;
1207	    using (_logger.BeginScope(new { CorrelationId = correlationId })) {
1208	        await next();
1209	    }
1210	});
1211	```
1212	
1213	- Inbound `X-Correlation-Id` header is honored if present (frontend may set one for
1214	  user-reported bug tracking).
1215	- Absent → derived from `Activity.Current.Id`; falls back to a fresh GUID only if no
1216	  Activity is active (shouldn't happen with ASP.NET auto-instrumentation).
1217	- Echoed in the response header — already exposed via CORS `WithExposedHeaders`.
1218	
1219	### Distributed Tracing
1220	
1221	ASP.NET, `HttpClient`, and Dapper are auto-instrumented via OpenTelemetry packages —
1222	no manual code required for those layers. **Business-layer operations MUST be wrapped
1223	in custom spans** so a trace shows the work, not just the HTTP and SQL.
1224	
1225	```csharp
1226	// In Kanban.Business — one ActivitySource per project
1227	private static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Kanban.Business");
1228	
1229	public async Task<Card> MoveCardAsync(MoveCardCommand cmd) {
1230	    using var activity = Source.StartActivity("MoveCard");
1231	    activity?.SetTag("card.id", cmd.CardId);
1232	    activity?.SetTag("target.lane.id", cmd.TargetLaneId);
1233	    // ...
1234	}
1235	```
1236	
1237	- One `ActivitySource` per project (`Kanban.Business`, `Kanban.Api`,
1238	  `Kanban.AntiCorruption`). Domain has no tracing — domain logic is pure.
1239	- Tag values MUST follow the PII rules above — GUIDs and status codes only, never
1240	  emails or card content.
1241	- `activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, "...")` MUST be called when an
1242	  exception is caught and rethrown — otherwise the span shows green in the trace UI.
1243

1248	| Metric | Source | Type |
1249	|--------|--------|------|
1250	| `http.server.request.duration` | ASP.NET auto-instrumentation | histogram |
1251	| `kanban.db.query.duration` | Dapper interceptor / manual `Meter` | histogram |
1252	| `kanban.auth.failure` | Auth middleware | counter |

1263	        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
